- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 2022-11 to 2022-12).
- Forecasts show upward drift without sufficient mean reversion, suggesting lack of volatility or trend correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), model tends to overshoot and continue rising, failing to reflect subsequent pullback.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits diminishing sensitivity to recent low prices (e.g., 70–75 range) and overweights recent high prices (e.g., 80–85).
- In late 2022/early 2023, model fails to capture sharp upward moves (e.g., +10–15% spikes) and underestimates volatility.
- Forecasts show increasing bias toward higher values as the horizon extends (e.g., 30-day forecast consistently 5–10% above true outcome).
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-month or holiday effects) that influence price behavior.
- When true price drops sharply (e.g., 85→75), model fails to reflect this and continues upward trend.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with each new data point, even when true price is declining.
